description: Scaffold the Next.js (App Router, TypeScript) project and establish a green baseline: linting, type checking, unit testing (Vitest), Tailwind styling, and a Vercel-ready configuration. This is the foundation every later feature builds on. Node must be loaded via nvm (`source ~/.nvm/nvm.sh && nvm use 22`) before any npm command.
steps: Initialize a Next.js 14+ App Router TypeScript project in the iq-study repo root (do not create a nested subfolder). Use `npx create-next-app@latest . --ts --app --tailwind --eslint --src-dir --import-alias "@/*" --no-turbopack` or equivalent manual scaffold. Ensure files land directly in iq-study/ (the repo root), not a subdirectory.

Add Vitest for unit testing: install vitest, @vitejs/plugin-react, and jsdom. Create vitest.config.ts configured for the @/* alias and a node/jsdom environment. Add npm scripts: "test": "vitest run", "test:watch": "vitest", "typecheck": "tsc --noEmit".
Add a trivial passing sanity unit test (e.g. src/lib/__tests__/sanity.test.ts) to confirm the Vitest pipeline runs.

Create .env.example documenting all env vars the app will use: OPENAI_API_KEY (optional; empty => mock AI provider), LLM_PROVIDER (openai|mock, default mock when no key), AUTH_SECRET (for session signing). Add a short comment per var.
Ensure .gitignore covers node_modules, .next, .env*.local, and any local dev DB files (e.g. *.sqlite, data/).

Create a minimal home page (src/app/page.tsx) with the app name 'IQ Study' and a short tagline describing the flow (upload a book -> analyze -> high-probability questions -> personalized adaptive study). Keep it simple; later features add real navigation.
Set next.config.mjs to a clean default that is Vercel-compatible.
acceptance_criteria: Running `source ~/.nvm/nvm.sh && nvm use 22 && npm install` succeeds with no errors.
`npm test` runs Vitest and the sanity test passes.
`npm run build` produces a successful Next.js production build.
.env.example exists and documents OPENAI_API_KEY, LLM_PROVIDER, and AUTH_SECRET.
Project files are at the repo root (package.json in iq-study/, not a nested folder).
verification: source ~/.nvm/nvm.sh && nvm use 22 && npm run lint
source ~/.nvm/nvm.sh && nvm use 22 && npm run typecheck
source ~/.nvm/nvm.sh && nvm use 22 && npm run build
findings: Scaffolded with `create-next-app@latest .` which installed Next.js 16.3.3 / React 19 (satisfies 'Next.js 14+'). create-next-app refuses to run in a dir containing .agents/, so .agents was temporarily moved out; /tmp got cleaned mid-run so the task-state files were restored from Kiro session snapshots (they are intact and committed). Node must be loaded via `source ~/.nvm/nvm.sh && nvm use 22` before any npm command. next.config was created as next.config.mjs (deleted the scaffold's next.config.ts). vitest.config was named vitest.config.mts (not .ts) to avoid a Vite CJS/ESM warning. Scaffold's .gitignore uses `.env*`; added `!.env.example` so the example env file is tracked, plus *.sqlite/*.db//data/ for local dev DB files. `--no-turbopack` only affects `next dev` in Next 16; `next build` still uses Turbopack by default and is Vercel-compatible. create-next-app also generated AGENTS.md + CLAUDE.md (regenerated by `next dev`); committed them to keep the tree clean. All verification passed: npm install, npm run lint, npm run typecheck, npm test (1 sanity test passing), npm run build (successful production build).
